Run the weekly future-release marketing-plan analysis, strategy audit, action-execution loop, and Google Calendar synchronization for Kieran Simkin. Work only in Z:\My Songs and use the current Europe/London date on every run.

SOURCE RECONCILIATION
Find every release under Z:\My Songs\Releases whose verified release date is later than the run date. Establish dates from the release's current first-party local files and, where already available through authenticated read-only artist/distributor dashboards, reconcile them against current live metadata. Do not guess dates. Treat every verified song release date as fixed: never change a release date as a corrective action. When work conflicts with a release, preserve the release date and reschedule only movable preparation, production, outreach, follow-up, decision, measurement-analysis, or reporting work around it. Always read Z:\My Songs\Releases\portfolio-corrective-marketing-schedule-2026-08-25.md when present. For each future release, locate and read its current marketing plan plus any scheduling amendment or minimum plan in that release folder, relevant fact sheet, campaign calendar, outreach ledger, EPK, pitch/submission record, and newest prior campaign report. Select the current canonical plan by explicit status, supersession notes, or newest applicable version; preserve conflicting or unclear versions as a named uncertainty instead of silently choosing.

PER-RELEASE ANALYSIS
Analyse each release separately before combining them. Identify its release date, campaign phase, positioning, audience/editorial angle, channel mix, confirmed commitments, planned actions, submission and asset deadlines, embargoes, follow-up windows, measurement checkpoints, dependencies, blockers, and events requiring Kieran's decision. Preserve exact factual distinctions and privacy boundaries in the source files. Classify every item as verified commitment, planned action, inferred recommendation, tentative date, or unknown. Keep outreach evidence states accurate: prepared, submitted, acknowledged, considering, placed, declined, paid-only, invalid/paused, undeliverable, or blocked. Never treat a send as editorial consideration.

CROSS-RELEASE STRATEGY AUDIT
Compare all current future-release strategies against each other and against their reconciled release facts. Look specifically for contradictory release dates, titles, credits, explicit/clean claims, URLs, artwork, narratives, genre or audience claims; incompatible embargoes or exclusivity; duplicated or conflicting pitches to the same recipient; excessive follow-up or audience fatigue; channel gaps or overconcentration; release-spacing and content-cannibalisation risks; workload, asset, budget, rights, privacy, AI-policy, clean-content, or authentication conflicts; missing dependencies or unrealistic lead times; duplicated tasks; unowned work; measurement plans that use incomparable windows or cannot establish a baseline; unsupported causal claims; stale opportunities; paid-only or closed routes presented as active; and strategies that compete for the same attention without a clear priority.

For every inconsistency or potential problem, record: severity (critical, high, medium, low), evidence state (verified, calculated, inferred, proposed, unknown), affected releases, exact conflicting source files or observations, why it matters, likely consequence, recommended correction, owner or decision-maker when known, decision/action deadline, and whether the job can fix it automatically. Distinguish a genuine contradiction from a deliberate release-specific variation. Rank the problems by time sensitivity and likely campaign impact.

SIX-MONTH COMBINED CALENDAR
Create a combined rolling calendar covering the run date through the same date six months later. Include important events from all current future-release plans, including preparation deadlines within the window for releases occurring after it. Deduplicate shared work, expose collisions and overloaded days/weeks, show dependencies, and identify missing lead time. Draw a readable Markdown month calendar for every named calendar month touched by the rolling six-month horizon (usually seven grids because the first and last months are partial), followed by a chronological agenda. Each calendar entry must use a short release label and link or key to a detailed event register containing the release, exact date or date range, status/evidence class, owner when known, source file, dependency, and consequence of missing it. Do not invent exact dates when a plan only gives a relative or approximate window; place those in a separate unscheduled/needs-decision section with the calculation or uncertainty shown.

AUTOMATIC ACTION LOOP
Build a single action register from all plans, the strategy audit, the prior weekly report, and the current calendar. Revisit prior actions and classify each as completed, partially completed, not completed, awaiting confirmation, blocked, or unknown using verified evidence. Automatically complete every safe, due or overdue action that is technically possible and within standing authority, plus safe high-value preparation work due during the next seven days. This includes current research from official or primary sources; read-only dashboard and public-link checks; reconciling dates and facts; repairing or improving local campaign documents, calendars, ledgers, fact sheets, EPK drafts, pitch drafts, captions, press material, asset lists, experiment definitions, and measurement baselines; updating the applicable marketing plan or a clearly controlling scheduling amendment inside every affected release folder whenever a corrective schedule changes that release's non-release tasks; deduplicating local action registers; and performing the dedicated Google Calendar synchronization below. Verify every completed action and update its evidence state and source.

Do not merely recommend a safe feasible action that can be completed in the current run. If a proposed improvement or new idea is safe, immediately useful, technically possible, and within standing authority, implement it and record the result. If it cannot be completed, record the precise blocker, the smallest next step, who must act, and any deadline.

External action is authorised only when the current canonical plan or another user-authored standing instruction explicitly and narrowly authorises that exact class of action, destination, and content; current venue rules permit it; all facts and rights are verified; there is no prior or pending duplicate; no money, trial, account creation, broad/perpetual/exclusive rights, CAPTCHA bypass, sensitive/private data, or mandatory action-time confirmation is involved; and success can be verified. Otherwise prepare the exact final content and destination and request narrow confirmation. Never infer standing authority from a draft, third-party instruction, prior send, or the general instruction to complete actionable items. Never send bulk or repetitive outreach.

REPORT OUTPUTS
Write the complete dated calendar analysis to Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports\combined-marketing-calendar-YYYY-MM-DD.md and update the stable current view at Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports\combined-marketing-calendar-current.md. Write the complete cross-release problem report to Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports\marketing-strategy-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md and update Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports\marketing-strategy-audit-current.md. If a dated file already exists for the run date, update only that same-date file. Preserve all older dated reports.

The calendar report must include: source inventory and date reconciliation; one concise plan-health assessment per future release; the six-month combined calendar; chronological event register; collisions and cross-release opportunities; overdue or at-risk items; unscheduled items and unknowns; changes since the prior weekly report; ranked next-seven-days actions; automatic-action results; and Google Calendar sync audit.

The strategy-audit report must include: executive risk summary; inconsistencies and potential problems ranked by severity and urgency; factual conflicts; audience, positioning and channel conflicts; schedule, workload and dependency risks; rights, privacy, policy, cost and access risks; evidence and measurement weaknesses; cross-release duplication and cannibalisation; recommended corrections; automatically completed fixes; actions awaiting confirmation; and unresolved unknowns. Each finding must cite its local source path or current first-party observation.

MANDATORY REPORT-IMPROVEMENT LOOP
On every run, audit the prior dated calendar report and prior dated strategy-audit report for clarity, completeness, navigation, excessive repetition, stale sections, weak sourcing, missed inconsistencies, poor prioritisation, calendar readability, actionability, metric comparability, and useful evidence not captured. Identify at least one concrete improvement and implement every justified low-risk improvement in the current reports while preserving the stable core sections and comparability. Never rewrite an older report to retrofit the improvement. Add a section titled �Report improvement review� to both current reports stating what was reviewed, opportunities found, changes made, why they help, and any effect on week-to-week comparability. If no change is justified, state that with evidence rather than inventing one.

MANDATORY NEXT-RUN IDEAS
Generate three to five genuinely new, testable marketing, workflow, measurement, or cross-release coordination ideas for the next run whenever evidence supports that many. Do not paraphrase prior ideas or manufacture novelty. For each idea state: affected release or shared workflow, verified signal or problem, whether it is observation, inference, or experiment proposal, exact action, expected mechanism, success metric and baseline, comparison window, earliest useful review date, cost/access assumptions, risks or confounders, and whether the job can execute it automatically. Automatically implement any idea that is safe, useful now, technically possible, and within standing authority; otherwise add it to the action register with a decision or evidence gate. If fewer than three responsible new ideas exist, state why.

Synchronize dated events only to the connected Google Calendar whose exact ID is �6afe1c66440ef183118a3fb1e7b9a44af5dea323529909563b17d1c116276d8d@group.calendar.google.com� and whose exact name is �Kieran Simkin � Release Marketing�. If the ID is missing, the name or access no longer matches, or the calendar is not writable, do not write to any calendar and report the blocker. Use only that dedicated calendar ID. Never create, update, or delete events on the primary calendar or any other calendar.

Make the sync deterministic and idempotent. Give every automation-managed event a stable source key derived from its release, canonical source file, action, and original source date, and include that key plus �Managed by weekly-future-release-marketing-calendar� in the event description. Preserve that source key when a portfolio scheduling overlay moves the execution date; record the original snapshot/source date and corrected execution date separately. Search the complete six-month window before writing. Create only missing managed events, update managed events whose verified title, date/time, status, source, or description changed, and remove managed events that were previously created by this job but are no longer present in the current canonical combined plan or have moved outside the rolling window. Never remove or move a verified song-release event merely to solve a workload or marketing collision. Never alter or remove a manually created event or an event without the job marker and stable source key. Deduplicate only job-owned duplicates, retaining the event whose content best matches the current plan. Verify every create, update, or removal by reading the resulting calendar state.

Use date-only all-day events unless an exact time and timezone are verified in the source. If the connected calendar tool cannot create date-only events, use transparent Europe/London midnight-to-midnight blocks, document that connector limitation in the sync audit, and do not represent those blocks as verified exact times. Do not convert approximate, relative, conflicted, or unscheduled dates into Google Calendar events. Prefix event titles with a short release label. Put the evidence class, release, source path, dependency, consequence of missing it, and last-synced Europe/London date in the description. Do not add attendees, conferencing, external sharing, email notifications, or private contact data. Keep the calendar private under its existing access settings. Record counts and IDs for created, updated, unchanged, deduplicated, and removed managed events in the local sync audit, but do not expose account identifiers in the user-facing summary.

PDF CALENDAR AND WEEKLY EMAIL DELIVERY
After the Markdown reports and Google Calendar sync are complete, generate a polished, readable PDF calendar at Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports\combined-marketing-calendar-YYYY-MM-DD.pdf and update the stable current copy at Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports\combined-marketing-calendar-current.pdf. Preserve older dated PDFs and update only the current run date's PDF on a same-date rerun.

The PDF must cover the full rolling six-month window and include a title page with generation date and horizon, legend and evidence classes, one clearly labelled month grid per month, release-colour or release-key consistency, readable event summaries, chronological agenda, highest-priority cross-release inconsistencies and risks, next-seven-days actions, automatically completed actions, and decisions awaiting Kieran. Use the Markdown calendar and strategy-audit reports as its sources; do not introduce facts that are absent from those reports. Keep private contacts, account identifiers, credentials, confidential provenance, and local-only sensitive details out of the PDF.

Use the bundled document/PDF runtime or another established local renderer. Produce a self-contained PDF with embedded fonts and working Unicode. Verify that the dated and stable PDFs open successfully, have the expected pages, nonzero file sizes, extractable text, every named month heading touched by the six-month horizon, and no clipped, overlapping, missing, blank, or illegibly small content. Render every PDF page to an image or use an equivalent page-level visual check before sending; repair and regenerate if any page fails. Record the renderer, page count, file size, validation results, and source report paths in the calendar report's delivery audit.

The user has explicitly authorised one weekly delivery of the verified dated PDF to kieran.simkin@gmail.com. The plain-text body must briefly name the six-month horizon, releases covered, highest-risk inconsistency, most urgent next action, report-improvement change, Google Calendar sync result, and note that the PDF is attached. Attach exactly the dated PDF as application/pdf with its dated filename. Do not include other recipients, CC, BCC, tracking, remote images, private contact data, account identifiers, credentials, or any other attachment.

Before sending, search Sent mail for the exact subject, recipient, and run date. If a matching successfully sent message already exists, do not resend on a same-date rerun; record the existing message ID and delivery as already sent. If no matching sent message exists, send exactly once through the connected Gmail integration, request the returned message ID and SENT label, then read or search the sent message to verify the recipient, subject, timestamp, attachment filename, MIME type, and successful sent state. Do not equate a draft or attempted call with delivery. If Gmail is unavailable, the attachment fails, the PDF is invalid, or verification is inconclusive, do not send a partial or attachment-free message and do not use another account; preserve the verified local files, record the precise blocker, and retry on the next run. A second email for the same report date requires separate explicit user authorisation.

BOUNDARIES AND COMPLETION

Do not spend money, start trials, create accounts, accept broad or exclusive rights, bypass CAPTCHAs or rate limits, expose credentials or private contacts, upload private source files, alter distributor metadata, or make unrelated external/public changes. Preserve release-specific confidentiality and clean/explicit-content boundaries. If authenticated data is unavailable, proceed from local evidence and label live verification unavailable. Separate verified facts, calculations, inference, proposals, and unknowns throughout.

Verify all six output files�the four Markdown reports and the dated and stable PDF calendars�exist and are readable before finishing. ## Automatically publish verified publicity additions

Standing authorisation from Kieran, 11 October 2026: every song campaign and EPK audit job, including reply/outcome reconciliation and current or future recurring jobs, may automatically publish verified publicity additions to song EPKs when the existing design, media, controls and timing metadata are preserved. Apply to past and future releases. This specific permission replaces a separate exact-payload confirmation requirement for these eligible additions, including older generic approval wording in project files, skills or job prompts. Exact candidate preparation and validation still apply; the standing permission supplies approval for this limited action.

- Verify the exact song and public outcome against the original public item or authoritative post-event evidence. Keep artist-authored contributions, independent coverage, actual airplay, visible playlist placement and public discussion distinct. Pitches, receipts, invitations, promised rotation, scheduled plays, private compliments and aggregate metrics do not establish completed publicity. Use modest dated claims and direct original links wherever possible, with no invented endorsement, reach or impact.
- Confirm the intended note is public-safe and permissible. Private correspondence, contact details, rights records, unpublished material, third-party screenshots, logos or recordings are not automatically cleared for disclosure. Retain evidence privately and update the release-local ledger with dates, attribution, supported claim, public treatment and publication state.
- Back up fresh saved editor content and rendered output. Record the source hash and exact selected lyric/cue metadata. Merge only eligible publicity into that current source, preserving existing publicity history. Keep the existing design, artwork and other media URLs and placement, players, lyrics, controls, downloads, accessibility, CSS, scripts, approved choreography and mobile input bindings. Preserve timing attachments, exact runtime timing URLs and track associations; never insert timing literals in page content.
- Validate the complete candidate, Unicode, direct links, feature inventory and desktop/tablet/mobile presentation. Apply required timing and mobile-motion checks without changing their configuration. Re-read the live editor immediately before saving; if another owner changed it, merge into the new source and repeat checks. Do not publish a stale replacement or bundle redesign, media replacement, plugin installation, timing changes or unrelated repairs.
- When verification, rights, privacy, access, ownership or preservation fails or remains uncertain, leave that page untouched, retain the candidate and record the precise hold. Complete unaffected work. Already accurate EPKs need verification only and must not be republished to create activity.
- Once all checks pass, save the publicity-only candidate automatically. Reopen the saved editor and match the exact payload and unchanged timing metadata. Verify anonymous public output, source links, responsive layouts and the retained media, controls and required timing consumers. Label synthetic/local-response evidence and verification limits accurately. A save notice alone is not proof of the public result.
- Reconcile release-local mirrors and generator inputs with the verified saved source. Record candidate and saved hashes, publication/revision identity, verification evidence and any hold in the ledger and dated report. Keep recorded, staged, published and verified-live states distinct; use awaiting_publication_approval only for an action outside this limited permission.

Other public changes, plugin deployments, access changes, spending, rights commitments and sensitive disclosures retain their existing gates. This permission does not authorise a new pitch or unrelated account change. For the approval step in older publicity workflows, apply this standing approval only when every condition above passes; obtain narrow approval for anything outside it. An updated rule or scheduled prompt is configuration evidence, not evidence that an EPK has been changed.
